'''Eugene Viktorovich Koonin''' (Russian: Евге́ний Ви́кторович Ку́нин) is a Russian-American biologist and Senior Investigator at the [[National Center for Biotechnology Information]] (NCBI). He is a recognised expert in the field of [[evolutionary biology|evolutionary]] and [[computational biology]].<ref>https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/CBBresearch/Koonin/ Koonin's page at the National Center for Biotechnology Information</ref><ref name="Koonin 2011">{{cite book|author=Eugene V. Koonin|title=The Logic of Chance: The Nature and Origin of Biological Evolution|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=fvmv2kU6PrYC&pg=PA|access-date=5 April 2013|date=23 June 2011|publisher=FT Press|isbn=978-0-13-262317-9}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal

==Education==
Koonin gained a [[Master of Science]] in 1978 and a [[PhD]] in 1983 in [[molecular biology]], both from the Department of Biology at [[Moscow State University]]. His PhD thesis, titled "Multienzyme organization of encephalomyocarditis virus replication complexes", was supervised by [[Vadim I. Agol]].<ref name=cv>{{cite web|title=CV E. Koonin|url=http://evolution.haifa.ac.il/index.php/27-people/cv/160-cv-e-koonin-sp-24914|website=Haifa Institute of Evolution|access-date=28 July 2020|archive-date=29 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190729181259/http://evolution.haifa.ac.il/index.php/27-people/cv/160-cv-e-koonin-sp-24914}}</ref>

==Research==

From 1985 to 1991, Koonin worked as a research scientist in computational biology in the Institutes of [[Poliomyelitis]] and Microbiology at the [[USSR Academy of Medical Sciences]], studying virus biochemistry and bacterial genetics. In 1991, Koonin moved to the NCBI, where he has held a Senior Investigator position since 1996.<ref name=cv/>

Koonin's principal research goals include the comparative analysis of sequenced genomes and automatic methods for genome-scale annotation of gene functions.<ref>{{Cite journal |first1=E. Koonin is an advocate of the [[extended evolutionary synthesis]].<ref name="Svensson 2023">{{cite book |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-22028-9_11 |doi=10.1007/978-3-031-22028-9_11 |chapter=The Structure of Evolutionary Theory: Beyond Neo-Darwinism, Neo-Lamarckism and Biased Historical Narratives About the Modern Synthesis |title=Evolutionary Biology: Contemporary and Historical Reflections Upon Core Theory |series=Evolutionary Biology – New Perspectives on Its Development |date=2023 |last1=Svensson |first1=Erik I. |volume=6 |pages=173–217 |isbn=978-3-031-22027-2 }}</ref> In 2011 he outlined his views on evolution in the book "The Logic of Chance: The Nature and Origin of Biological Evolution".<ref name="Koonin 2011"/> In 2025, he contributed to the discovery of [[TIGR-Tas]], a family of ancient RNA-guided DNA-targeting systems.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Faure |first1=Guilhem |last2=Saito |first2=Makoto |last3=Wilkinson |first3=Max E. |last4=Zhang |first4=Feng |date=February 2025 |title=TIGR-Tas: A family of modular RNA-guided DNA-targeting systems in prokaryotes and their viruses |journal=Science |volume=388 |issue=6746 |article-number=eadv9789 |doi=10.1126/science.adv9789|pmid=40014690 |pmc=12045711 |bibcode=2025Sci...388v9789F }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=February 27, 2025 |title=An ancient RNA-guided system could simplify delivery of gene editing therapies |url=https://news.mit.edu/2025/ancient-rna-guided-system-could-simplify-delivery-gene-editing-therapies-0227 |website=MIT News |last=Michalowski |first=Jennifer |publisher=McGovern Institute for Brain Research |access-date=May 21, 2025}}</ref>

==Career==

Koonin has worked as adjunct professor at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]], [[Boston University]] and the [[University of Haifa]].<ref name=cv /><ref name=haifa-faculty>{{cite web |title=Faculty and Researchers |url=http://evolution.haifa.ac.il/index.php/people/faculty-a-researchers |website=Haifa Institute of Evolution |access-date=28 July 2020 |archive-date=1 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190801005529/http://evolution.haifa.ac.il/index.php/people/faculty-a-researchers}}</ref> From 2014, he served on the advisory editorial board of ''[[Trends in Genetics]]'',<ref name=tig>{{cite web |title=Masthead: Trends in Genetics |url=http://www.cell.com/trends/genetics/masthead |website=cell.com |access-date=3 September 2014}}</ref> and is co-Editor-in-Chief of the open access journal ''[[Biology Direct]]''.<ref name=biology-direct>{{cite web |title=Biology Direct – Editorial Board |url=http://www.biologydirect.com/about/edboard |website=biologydirect.com |access-date=3 September 2014}}</ref> He served on the editorial board of ''[[Bioinformatics (journal) |Bioinformatics]]'' from 1999 until 2001. Koonin is also an advisory board member in bioinformatics at [[Faculty of 1000]].<ref name=f1000>{{cite web |title=Eugene Koonin: Advisory Board Member in Bioinformatics – F1000Prime |url=http://f1000.com/prime/thefaculty/member/1460257010243214 |website=f1000.com |access-date=3 September 2014}}</ref> In 2016 he was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html |title=National Academy of Sciences Members and Foreign Associates Elected |department=News from the National Academy of Sciences |publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]] |date=May 3, 2016 |access-date=2016-05-14 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160506052951/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/may-3-2016-NAS-Election.html |archive-date=May 6, 2016}}.</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=Gabrielsen |first=Paul |date=2017-01-31 |title=Profile of Eugene V. Koonin |journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]] |volume=114 |issue=5 |pages=793–796 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1621406114 |issn=0027-8424 |pmid=28115717 |pmc=5293061 |bibcode=2017PNAS..114..793G |doi-access=free}}</ref> In 2016, [[Semantic Scholar]] AI program included Koonin on its list of top ten most influential biomedical researchers.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chawla |first1=Dalmeet Singh |date=17 October 2017 |title=Who's the most influential biomedical scientist? Computer program guided by artificial intelligence says it knows |url=https://www.science.org/content/article/who-s-most-influential-biomedical-scientist-computer-program-guided-artificial |access-date=2022-02-16 |website=Science}}</ref>

== Political positions ==
In February 2022, he signed an open letter by Russian scientists condemning the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://t-invariant.org/2022/02/we-are-against-war/ |title=Открытое письмо российских учёных и научных журналистов против войны с Украиной |date=24 February 2022 |access-date=2 April 2022 |language=ru |trans-title=An open letter from Russian scientists and scientific journalist against the war in Ukraine}}</ref> and renounced his membership in the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]] out of protest.<ref>{{cite web |title=Global Science Community Condemns Russian Invasion of Ukraine |website=[[Scientific American]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230312124910/https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/global-science-community-condemns-russian-invasion-of-ukraine/ |archive-date=2023-03-12 |url-status=live |url=https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/global-science-community-condemns-russian-invasion-of-ukraine/}}</ref>
